governed_construct: Use of a front-end UI/reactivity framework in a code unit: an import (static, dynamic or require) of a UI framework package or its ecosystem sub-packages (vue, vue-router, pinia, react, react-dom, preact, svelte, solid-js, @angular/core, ...), or JSX whose factory/import source is a UI framework (resolved through the jsxImportSource pragma or compiler configuration). Each such framework binding or JSX usage is one instance.
interpretation: 'Use Vue' is read as: whenever a code unit builds UI components, reactive state, app bootstrap or routing with a front-end framework, that framework must be Vue (the 'vue' package or Vue-ecosystem packages such as vue-router and pinia). A unit that imports and uses Vue APIs (defineComponent, ref, computed, createApp, h, composables, Vue router) is SATISFIED. A unit that uses React, Preact, Svelte, SolidJS, Angular or another UI framework is VIOLATED, even if it also uses Vue. A unit with no UI-framework usage at all (plain utility code) is NOT_APPLICABLE. JSX/TSX is not itself a violation: JSX conforms when its factory resolves to Vue (via '@jsxImportSource vue', Vue's JSX plugin with defineComponent render functions) and violates when it resolves to React or another framework; deciding this needs the JSX import source and the bindings of imported names, which is why the rule is T3.
